title: AI / Inference serving
description: How fast the served model is running, what it is holding and how close it is to a limit. Opens on the last 15 minutes at one-second detail and refreshes every five seconds.

panels.title: Serving identity
panels.description: Labels identify the model, recipe, runtime and host on each successful scrape younger than ten seconds.

panels.title: Engine
panels.description: The engine's own health flag. Broken means a fault has stopped it serving; /health gives the first cause.

panels.title: Scrape
panels.description: Successful inference metrics scrape younger than ten seconds, shown per serving host. This does not prove a request can complete.

panels.title: Running
panels.description: Current requests in prefill or decode. This counts requests, not TP ranks.

panels.title: Waiting
panels.description: Native queued/held requests. Does not expose queue-wait duration or failed requests.

panels.title: Live output
panels.description: Generated tokens across all streams, finished and in flight, over the last ten seconds. Includes idle time and is not decode speed per reply.

panels.title: Pool used
panels.description: Share of the shared context pool held by streams and kept prompts. Kept prompts are evicted as it fills, so a high figure means less reuse before it means failure.

panels.title: Output throughput
panels.description: Tokens written across all streams, as they are written. The trace follows the zoom; the trend is a one-minute slope. Includes idle time.

panels.title: Decode speed per reply
panels.description: Tokens per second of each reply's own decode time, averaged over finished requests. Concurrent replies share the GPU, so this falls as more run; the total is Output throughput.

panels.title: Prefill speed · new tokens
panels.description: Prompt tokens not found in cache, per second of prefill time, over finished requests. Cached tokens are left out, since they take no prefill.

panels.title: Time to first token
panels.description: Server arrival to first generated token. Counts of finished requests in each latency bucket, one column per step of at least a minute. Buckets above ten seconds are wide: 30, 60, 120 and 300 s.

panels.title: Request latency
panels.description: Server arrival to reply completion. Counts of finished requests in each latency bucket, one column per step of at least a minute. Buckets above ten seconds are wide: 30, 60, 120 and 300 s.

panels.title: Mean latency
panels.description: Mean over finished requests. Both are recorded at completion; time to first token ends at the first generated token, not necessarily the first text a client sees.

panels.title: Running and waiting requests
panels.description: Requests in prefill or decode, and requests queued or held until a lane is free, against the streams the engine runs at once. TP ranks are not extra requests.

panels.title: Completed requests
panels.description: Requests finished in each step, of at least a minute. The step grows as the range does, so compare heights only within one view.

panels.title: Prompt cache hits
panels.description: Share of prompt tokens found cached, over finished requests.

panels.title: Pool and fullest stream
panels.description: Pool used is the shared cache held by streams and kept prompts. Fullest stream is the largest live stream's share of its own context window; it is zero while idle. Neither is host memory.

panels.title: Prompt tokens read
panels.description: Prompt tokens of finished requests, stacked. Only the new ones take prefill time, and all are booked at completion rather than while prefill runs. A recipe that reports no cache shows one unsplit total.

panels.title: Decode round time
panels.description: Milliseconds of decode per round, averaged over finished requests. It rises as more replies run at once, and unlike tokens per second it does not move with draft acceptance.

panels.title: Speculative acceptance
panels.description: Accepted divided by drafted tokens across finished requests. No value when no drafts were verified.

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: Inference metrics scrape duration, with an 800 ms timeout and one-second interval. The scrape makes no inference request.

options.content: A successful scrape does not prove a request can complete. Decode and prefill speed average finished requests, so they lag a running reply. Client-visible latency, queue-wait duration and error or cancellation counts remain unmeasured. See the [monitoring runbook](https://github.com/kelchm/home-lab/blob/main/sparks/monitoring/README.md).
